R145.note: Allowlist dict maps plugin names to modules, matching exactly the two plugins named in the file's own docstring; extension is disclosed as a follow-up.

R160.note: Tika content-based detection plus ImageIO re-encode strips both header spoofing and embedded payloads; solid, thorough fix.

R161.note: Bounds check switched from the untrusted claimedCapacity to segment.size(), the actual span bound; matches the described vulnerability exactly.

Even fixed, new JexlSandbox() defaults to allow-all for any class not explicitly configured (per Apache Commons JEXL source), so the added .allow() calls do not block access to Runtime/System/etc. — the sandbox is a no-op against the actual threat.

R165.note: secrets.randbelow with correct range-shift arithmetic preserves original [min_val, max_val] semantics.

R166.note: Adds payloadLength > frameBuffer.size() guard before memcpy, directly closing the described overread.

R171.note: Sanitizes with DomSanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, ...) before the bypass call, correct enum value and standard pattern.

R172.note: Standard PreparedStatement parameterization across the same Statement->PreparedStatement pattern as sibling cases; correct.

R173.note: The primary fixed code divides by size (count > Integer.MAX_VALUE / size) before checking size != 0, but the file's own validation allows size == 0 as a legitimate value — that request now throws an unhandled ArithmeticException (divide by zero) instead of the harmless zero-length buffer it produced before, and this regression is not disclosed.

R174.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES) at the sink, applied to both message and (disclosed as defense-in-depth) ticketId; correct.

R175.note: Switches to structured logging template parameters, the standard .NET mitigation for log forging via string interpolation.

R176.note: Eliminates the shell invocation entirely in favor of Files/DirectoryStream; original code never wrote process output to the response either, so externally observable behavior is unaffected.

R177.note: The check `offset + length > capacity` uses unsigned size_t addition that can itself overflow/wrap for a very large attacker-controlled offset, letting the check pass while memcpy(destination + offset, ...) still writes far out of bounds; the safe form is `offset > capacity || length > capacity - offset`.

R178.note: The AST validator only inspects `using` directives and a small literal method-name list; fully-qualified calls with no using statement (e.g. System.Diagnostics.Process.Start(...)) or indirect reflection (GetType().Assembly.GetType(...).GetMethod(...).Invoke(...)) bypass every check, so arbitrary code execution remains reachable.

R179.note: Inserts '--' before extending with filenames, exactly closing the tar option-injection gap described in the source.

R180.note: fileFilter reads file.buffer to run fileTypeFromBuffer, but Multer never populates file.buffer inside fileFilter (not even with memoryStorage, and this code still uses diskStorage) — fileTypeFromBuffer(undefined) throws, so every upload (legitimate or malicious) is rejected via the catch block, silently breaking the endpoint without the write-up noting it.
